subject: Usage-banded discount proposal and migration credit — next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage-banded discount proposal and migration credit — next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time last Tuesday. Based on our conversation and the preliminary usage data you shared, I attached an updated pricing sheet that shifts the discount model from a flat seat discount to a usage-banded approach (see attachment: usage-band-pricing-v2.xlsx). The goal is to better align unit economics with Clearline's bursty inference profile and give you more upside as consumption scales.

Quick summary of the change:
- Small band (0–1M tokens/month): 10% off list
- Mid band (1–5M tokens/month): 18% off list
- High band (5M+ tokens/month): 28% off list

Separately, we're proposing a one-time migration credit to cover migration engineering and runbook work: $40k applied as credits over the first 3 billing cycles. That can be structured as a one-time invoice credit or amortized against monthly usage — whichever helps procurement.

Can you confirm:
1) Whether procurement wants the credit structured as an invoice credit or contract-side creditline?
2) If legal needs a redline of the SOW, I attached a draft SOW (SOW-draft-clearline.pdf) — do you want us to iterate before we send to your procurement mailbox?

If this looks directionally right I can loop in your procurement contact and send a slightly tightened commercial to sign (DocuSign link) — otherwise happy to hop on another 30m call to walk through bands and the migration plan.

Best,

Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.p@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: usage-band-pricing-v2.xlsx, SOW-draft-clearline.pdf
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@clearlinehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@clearlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage-banded discount proposal and migration credit — next steps

Thanks Monica — this is helpful. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we loop procurement in: 

- The bands look reasonable but we need the effective per-token price for our top-line forecast (can you add an example line showing blended USD/month at 2.5M and 7.5M tokens?)
- Procurement typically prefers a contract-side credit (applied as a credit line) rather than an invoice-level rebate for audit purposes.
- We will need the SOW to call out data handling responsibilities during migration (esp. KV cache warm-up and any logs we may need to retain for 90 days). Can you surface that in the SOW?

I cc'd procurement so they're aware but please keep the first pass commercial to me until we confirm structure. Once we have the per-token examples and SOW callouts I can get a 1st-pass from procurement/legal.

Also looping in Tom (procurement) — Tom, quick heads up: Monica will send the contract-side credit structure + blended-pricing examples; appreciate a read and ballpark timeline for review.

— Samantha
VP, Product — Clearline Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Usage-banded discount proposal and migration credit — need pricing confirmation

Markus / Karthik —

Forwarding Sam's note (above). They prefer a contract-side credit and want blended examples for 2.5M and 7.5M tokens. Also need SOW language calling out data handling during the migration (KV cache warm-up, limited log retention 90d). Deal context: DL-9834, mid-market health prospect, expected year-one runrate if they hit mid-band ~ $420k ARR. Competitive pressure: incumbent is offering a 20% flat discount + 3 months free pilot seats. We need to make this defensible while preserving margin on usage.

My suggested commercial (draft numbers) — open to pushback: 
- Usage bands (as in the attached): 0–1M: 10% off list (per-token list $0.0025 -> effective $0.00225)
- 1–5M: 18% off list (effective per-token $0.00205)
- 5M+: 28% off list (effective per-token $0.0018)
- One-time migration credit: $40k applied as a contract credit, amortized equally over first 3 billing cycles; credit explicitly conditioned on completion of migration milestones (data ingest validation, KV warm-up, runbook handover).
- Optional pilot: 30-day pilot with up to 200k tokens/month free (to match their incumbent's 3 months free seats, this is smaller but targeted to runway).

Questions: 
1) Can finance/legal sign off on contract-side credit for DL-9834? We want to avoid invoicing complexity.
2) Markus — do the effective prices above hold up in your margin model if they start at mid-band? If not, what floor do you need?

If you both sign off I will prepare the blended examples and add the SOW callouts for data handling and send back to Samantha/procurement.

Thanks,
Monica

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Appended below are the blended pricing examples you asked for plus the SOW callouts we propose for migration responsibilities. I attached a tightened commercial and the SOW (SOW-draft-clearline.pdf) for legal review.

Blended examples (rounded):
- 2.5M tokens/month -> blended effective price = $0.00209/token -> ~$5,225/month
- 7.5M tokens/month -> blended effective price = $0.00186/token -> ~$13,950/month

Migration credit structure: $40k contract-side credit applied across first 3 invoices following go-live. Credit is tied to milestone acceptance: 
1) Data ingest validation (Clearline accepts sample ingest tests)
2) KV cache warm-up completed and verified (both teams sign off)
3) Runbook handover (operational runbook delivered, initial runbook walkthrough complete)

SOW callouts we added: 
- Data handling during migration: Redwood will not persist Clearline PII beyond transient processing required for migration; any debug logs containing PII will be redacted and kept no longer than 90 days unless otherwise requested.
- KV cache warm-up: Redwood will provide a cache-warmup plan and collaborate on a warm-up window to avoid tail latency impact; acceptance criteria are documented in section 3.2.
- Support handover: 30-day elevated support window post go-live, included.

If this is OK I'll convert the commercial into a contract-ready redline and send to your procurement mailbox (Tom) with the DocuSign link. If procurement prefers the credit amortized differently, we can update contract language — let me know the preference.

Next steps: 
- Samantha: confirm contract-side credit OK (your note earlier suggested yes)
- Tom: roughly how long for procurement/legal to review (we can accommodate a short review window if needed)
- If everyone aligns I'll route the DocuSign and target a 2-week review + 30-day pilot window.

Thanks!

Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
